breakfast.name: Bryndzové Halušky
instructions: Mix grated potato with flour, egg, salt
Press dough through spaetzle maker into boiling water
Drain, toss with bryndza cheese
Top with crispy bacon and chives
breakfast.description: Slovakia's national dish — potato dumplings with sheep cheese and bacon.

breakfast.name: Lokše (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Mix mashed potatoes with flour and salt
Roll thin
Cook on dry griddle
Spread with goose fat

breakfast.name: Pagac (Savory Dough Pastries)
instructions: Pagac are Slovak savory pastries -- made from yeast dough
Filled with cottage cheese or mashed potato
Brushed with egg and sprinkled with caraway seeds
Baked until golden
A Slovak bakery staple -- sold alongside bread
breakfast.description: Slovak savory yeast-dough pastries -- filled with cottage cheese or mashed potato, brushed with egg, sprinkled with caraway seeds, baked golden. A Slovak bakery staple sold alongside bread.

breakfast.name: Ovsena Kasa (Oatmeal Porridge)
instructions: Oatmeal porridge is the Slovak winter breakfast
Cooked in milk for richness
Can be sweet (with honey and dried fruit) or savory (with butter and salt)
The savory version with butter: the traditional Slovak way
breakfast.description: Slovak oatmeal porridge -- rolled oats cooked in milk, served savory with butter and salt (the traditional Slovak way) or sweet with honey. The winter breakfast.

lunch.name: Kapustnica (Sauerkraut Soup)
instructions: Sauté onion with paprika
Add sauerkraut and water
Add smoked meat and mushrooms
Simmer 45 min
Add cream before serving
lunch.description: Rich sauerkraut soup with smoked meats — a Christmas tradition.

lunch.name: Vyprážaný Syr (Fried Cheese)
instructions: Coat cheese in flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden
Serve with tartare sauce and fries
lunch.description: Breaded fried cheese with fries — Slovak comfort food.

lunch.name: Kapustnica (Sauerkraut Soup)
instructions: Kapustnica is the Slovak national soup -- served at Christmas Eve dinner
The Christmas Eve kapustnica: a tradition that no Slovak family skips
Sauerkraut gives the sourness
Smoked pork ribs give the smokiness
Dried mushrooms give the earthy depth
A complex, rich, deeply satisfying soup
lunch.description: Slovak Christmas Eve sauerkraut soup -- sauerkraut, smoked pork ribs, and dried mushrooms simmered with paprika and caraway seeds into a complex, rich, sour-smoky-earthy soup. Served at Christmas Eve dinner across Slovakia without exception.

lunch.name: Fazulova Polievka (Bean Soup)
instructions: Bean soup is the everyday Slovak soup
The beans are cooked with smoked pork
A flour-and-fat roux is used to thicken
Paprika gives the characteristic Slovak color and flavor
Sour cream stirred in at the end -- the Slovak finishing touch
lunch.description: Slovak bean soup -- white beans cooked with smoked pork, thickened with a roux, finished with sweet paprika and sour cream. The everyday Slovak soup.

lunch.name: Bryndzove Halusky (Sheep Cheese Dumplings)
instructions: Bryndzove halusky is the Slovak national dish
Halusky: small potato dumplings, made by pressing potato dough through a colander
The dumplings fall directly into boiling water
Bryndza: the Slovak sheep cheese -- aged, pungent, crumbly, slightly salty
The bryndza is tossed with the hot halusky
Smoked bacon fried until crispy is scattered over the top
The combination of the soft dumplings and the pungent cheese and crispy bacon
lunch.description: Slovak national dish -- small potato dumplings (halusky) pressed through a colander directly into boiling water, tossed with bryndza (pungent aged sheep cheese), topped with crispy smoked bacon. Bryndza is the Slovak cheese identity.

dinner.name: Segedin Goulash
instructions: Sauté onion, add paprika and caraway
Brown pork, add water
Simmer 40 min
Add sauerkraut, simmer 15 more min
Stir in cream
dinner.description: Pork goulash with sauerkraut and cream.

dinner.name: Pirohy (Pierogi)
ingredients: Filling: bryndza cheese, potato, or sauerkraut
instructions: Make dough, roll thin
Cut circles, fill
Pinch closed, boil until they float
Toss with butter
Top with bacon and sour cream
dinner.description: Slovak pierogi with bryndza or potato filling.

dinner.name: Segedinsky Gulas (Segedin Goulash)
instructions: Segedinsky gulas is the Slovak-Hungarian goulash with sauerkraut
Different from regular goulash: the sauerkraut is added
The sourness of the sauerkraut cuts through the richness of the paprika stew
Named after Jozef Segedinsky -- a Hungarian writer who allegedly requested it
The Slovak version differs slightly from the Hungarian original
dinner.description: Slovak-Hungarian sauerkraut goulash -- pork shoulder braised in paprika sauce with sauerkraut and caraway seeds, finished with sour cream. The sauerkraut sourness cuts the paprika richness. Named after Hungarian writer Jozef Segedinsky.

dinner.name: Svickova na Smetane (Beef in Cream Sauce)
ingredients: Root vegetables: carrot, parsley root, celery, onion
Cream sauce: heavy cream, butter, lemon juice
instructions: Svickova na smetane is a Slovak-Czech beef sirloin dish in cream sauce
The beef is marinated in vegetables and vinegar, then slow-braised
The vegetables and braising liquid are blended into the cream sauce
The cream sauce is characteristic: sweet, slightly acidic, aromatic
Served with bread dumplings and a spoonful of cranberry jam
The cranberry jam and lemon: the fruit accents against the rich sauce
dinner.description: Slovak beef in cream sauce -- beef sirloin slow-braised with root vegetables and vinegar, the braising liquid blended with cream into a sweet-acidic-aromatic sauce. Served with bread dumplings and cranberry jam. Shared with Czech cuisine.

dinner.name: Struklji (Strudel-Like Rolls)
ingredients: Cottage cheese filling (tvaroh + sugar + vanilla + raisins)
instructions: Struklji are the Slovak sweet cottage cheese rolls
Thin dough rolled with sweetened cottage cheese filling
Baked or boiled
Served with sour cream or melted butter
dinner.description: Slovak sweet cottage cheese rolls -- thin dough filled with sweetened tvaroh (cottage cheese), raisins, and vanilla, baked or boiled, served with sour cream or melted butter.

snacks.name: Pagáčiky (Cheese Biscuits)
instructions: Make dough with cheese and sour cream
Roll, fold layers
Cut rounds
Bake at 200°C 20 min

snacks.name: Ostiepok (Smoked Sheep Cheese)
ingredients: Ostiepok (traditional Slovak smoked sheep cheese -- the oval decorated form)
instructions: Ostiepok is the traditional Slovak smoked sheep cheese
Made in a distinctive oval or round shape, often with decorative patterns
EU protected designation: Ostiepok from Slovakia only
The cheese is made in the mountain sheep farming regions: Orava, Liptov
Smoked over beech wood -- the golden-brown exterior
The interior: elastic, semi-firm, slightly salty, smoky
snacks.description: Slovak protected smoked sheep cheese -- Ostiepok, made in distinctive decorative shapes in the mountain regions (Orava, Liptov), smoked over beech wood. EU-protected designation. Elastic, semi-firm, slightly salty, smoky interior.

snacks.name: Liptovsky Syr (Liptov Cheese Spread)
instructions: Liptauer is the Slovak cheese spread -- famous throughout Central Europe
Named after the Liptov region of Slovakia -- the sheep farming center
A spreadable seasoned cheese: bryndza or tvaroh base
Mixed with butter, onion, caraway, and paprika
A beloved spread on bread or crackers
snacks.description: Slovak Liptauer cheese spread -- bryndza (sheep cheese) base mixed with butter, onion, caraway seeds, and paprika into a spreadable condiment. Named after the Liptov region. Famous across Central Europe as a bread spread.

snacks.name: Zemiakove Placky (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Zemiakove placky are Slovak potato pancakes -- similar to but distinct from German Reibekuchen
Grated raw potato squeezed of moisture
Mixed with egg, a little flour, and aromatics
Fried in lard or oil until golden and crispy
The caraway seeds: the Slovak flavor
snacks.description: Slovak potato pancakes -- raw grated potato (squeezed dry) with egg, flour, garlic, and caraway seeds, fried in lard until golden and crispy. The caraway seeds distinguish the Slovak from the German version.

desserts.name: Šúľance (Sweet Dumplings)
instructions: Make potato dough, roll into ropes
Cut into pieces, boil until they float
Toss with butter, poppy seeds, sugar
desserts.description: Sweet potato dumplings rolled in poppy seeds and sugar.

desserts.name: Veternik (Cream Puff)
instructions: Veternik is the Slovak cream puff -- filled with vanilla cream and glazed with caramel
The classic Slovak pastry shop item
Choux pastry baked until hollow
Filled with smooth vanilla pastry cream
Topped with caramel glaze
desserts.description: Slovak cream puff -- choux pastry baked hollow, filled with vanilla pastry cream, topped with caramel glaze. The classic Slovak pastry shop item.

desserts.name: Trdelnik (Spiral Chimney Cake)
instructions: Trdelnik is the spiral pastry cooked over an open fire
The dough is wrapped around a wooden spit
Cooked over fire while rotating
The caramelized sugar and cinnamon crust forms on the outside
A Czech-Slovak street food -- now a Prague tourist icon
The Slovakian version predates the Prague tourist version
desserts.description: Slovak spiral chimney cake -- sweet yeast dough wrapped around a wooden spit, cooked over fire while rotating, the outside caramelizing with sugar and cinnamon. Rolled in ground walnuts. A traditional Slovak street food, the origin of the now-touristy Prague trdelnik.

drinks.name: Slivovica (Plum Brandy)
instructions: Ferment ripe plums
Distill twice in copper pot
Age at least 1 year
drinks.description: Strong plum brandy — Central European heritage spirit.

drinks.name: Kofola
instructions: Serve chilled
Slovakia's beloved cola alternative — herbal and less sweet
drinks.description: Slovak herbal cola — a national soft drink icon.

drinks.name: Kofola (Slovak Cola)
ingredients: Kofola (Slovak herbal cola -- with chicory, dandelion, malt, and herb extracts)
instructions: Kofola is the Slovak and Czech cola -- created in 1960 under communism
Invented to substitute for Western Coca-Cola which was unavailable
The recipe: chicory, dandelion, malt extract, and a proprietary herb blend
Deeply loved in Slovakia and Czech Republic -- outsells Coca-Cola in some regions
Served on tap (from the keg) -- the draught version is the authentic experience
Slightly less sweet than Coca-Cola, with a herbal complexity
drinks.description: Slovak communist-era herbal cola -- created in 1960 to substitute for Western Coca-Cola, using chicory, dandelion, malt, and a secret herb blend. Deeply loved in Slovakia and Czech Republic; outsells Coca-Cola in some regions. Best served on draught from the tap.
